objections.claim: The evaluated-commit rule remains unsound because it accepts a required check from EITHER the PR head or the synthetic test-merge commit. GitHub instead applies precedence: when the test-merge commit has a status, that commit must pass; only when it has no status may the head commit satisfy the requirement ([GitHub required-check documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks)). Under the proposed OR rule, a trusted green push-context run at the head can satisfy the controller while an untrusted app supplies the same-name green status on the synthetic merge commit that GitHub selects, permitting the server to merge without a trusted run testing the merge result. The controller must mirror GitHub's precedence per required context, authenticate the selected commit's producer, and include a regression combining a trusted green head run with an untrusted same-name synthetic-merge status.
